General Safety Procedures
Notes
Safety precautions need to be taken during installation and operation of any the
telecommunication equipment.
1. When installing the device always make the ground connection first. When
removing the device remove the ground connection at the end.
2. Do not block ventilation cavities of the working devices during installation or
maintenance of other devices
3. Avoid any operation/installation during lightning strikes.
4. Do not look directly into the optical port to prevent the injuries to your eyes
from laser rays.
5. When handling power related operational activities, do not wear conductive
articles, such as watches, hand chains, bracelets and rings.
6. Proper grounding of the devices is a must before power on.
7. Before installing or removing the power cable, turn off the power switches &
disconnect the cable from the power source end whenever possible.
8. Before connecting the power cable, confirm that the power cable and label
comply with the requirements of the actual installation
9. If a fuse is to be replaced, the new fuse shall be of the same type an
specifications.
10. The static electricity generated by the human body may damage the
electrostatic sensitive components on the circuit board. Before touching the
device, hand-operating parts, circuit boards, wear a grounded electrostatic
discharge (ESD) wrist strap.

Female Fast Connector (Pressfit Type)
1. Determine the length of the power cable for different operations based on

2. Strip the specified length of the sheath off the power cable.
3. Strip a specified length of sheath off each core wire. The length must be
consistent with the length of the notch in the female fast connector (pressfit

4. Connect the blue core wire labeled NEG(-) to the - port and the black/brown
core wire labeled RTN(+) to the + port on the female fast connector and then

1. Determine the length of the power cable for different operations based on the

2. Strip the specified length of the sheath off the power cable.
3. Strip the specified length of sheath off each core wire. Ensure that the length
of the sheath stripped off each core wire match the length of the female fast
connector (screw-free type).
4. Connect the blue core wire labeled NEG(-) to the "-" port and the black/brown
core wire labeled RTN(+) to the "+" port on the connector. Ensure that the
head of each core wire is in contact with the bottom of the terminal block so
that the clip can be automatically closed. The core wire is secured when you
hear a click.
5. After the core wires are installed, ensure that each core wire is securely
installed after being dragged with a force of 30 N (6.75 lbf) and all copper
wires are inserted in the connector terminal socket.

Waterproofing and Weatherproofing
Notes
1. Moisture build up within the RF/IF connectors can wreak havoc on a system’s
performance.
2. The coaxial cable’s dielectric is typically made of open-cell foam, which can
act like a sponge, absorbing and retaining moisture.
92
3. Moisture encourages corrosion around the connector, potentially leading to a
scenario where RF signals inadvertently mix and generate passive
intermodulation (PIM) distortion.
4. PIM can interfere with neighboring frequencies, prompting a host of legal and
regulatory headaches for the operator. Also, it will generate high VSWR values
and damage transmitter equipment at some point.
5. Common procedure for outdoor RF/IF connector water proofing…
a. Step 1- Vinyl insulation tapes should apply as the first layer. It should be
wrapped from top to Bottom to avoid draining water inward if the
mastic/Rubber tape layer is damaged at any position and water leaked in
to the seal.
b. Step 2- Then 2 layers of mastic/Scotch, typically made of butyl rubber
should be applied. This layer should form a seal against water intrusion,
completely covering the connector/joint.
c. Step 3- then 2 layers of Vinyl tape should be applied to secure the mastic
in place and protect it from UV rays. This wrapping also should begin from
the top and end on bottom side of the connection. The end product
should look like a smooth, round bump on the cable.
d. Finally, a tie wrap tighten at both ends of the sealing can ensure stability
of vinyl tape edge

can seep in, potentially resulting in service outages.

Battery Safety
Before installing, operating, or maintaining batteries, read the battery
manufacturer's instructions. The safety precautions specified in this document
151

Battery Installation
Before installing batteries, observe the following safety precautions:
1. Install batteries in a dry and cool environment with good ventilation, which is
away from high temperature and flammable materials, and take precautions
against fire.
2. Place and secure batteries horizontally.
3. Note the polarities when installing batteries. Do not short-circuit the positive
and negative poles of the same battery or battery string. Otherwise, the
battery may be short-circuited.
4. When installing a battery string, retain at least one breakpoint to prevent a
loop being formed. After checking that the installation is correct, close the
breakpoints to finish the installation.
5. During the installation, insulate the terminals of cables connecting batteries.
Ensure that the terminals do not come into contact with metal components
such as the cabinet.
6. Secure battery cables or copper bars by tightening bolts to the required
torque. Loose connections will result in excessive voltage drop or cause
batteries to burn out in the case of excessive current.
7. Check battery connections periodically, ensuring that all bolts are securely
tightened.

GSM Filter Installation
Introduction of GSM FILTER
The requirement for filter installation on 900 MHz band occurred due to receiver
blocking interference arises with LTE implementation in Band 5. Even though the
RRU specifications of Band 8 specifies the starting bandwidth as 880/890 (Band
8) due to imperfect filter cutoffs, RRU will be absorbing signal power outside from
its specified band.
Since these outside frequencies now corresponds to downlink of L850 cells, the
noise level for Band 8 RRU is higher than usual creating a blocking interference.
By applying filter on the receiver side, these unwanted signals from Band 5 will
be rejected at the RRU to maintain appropriate noise level.
Best Location to install GSM Filter
1. Mount on rear side of same antenna pole where space is available (free RRU).
2. If space is not available in same antenna, mount on adjacent pole.
3. Install at location where a man can stand and access working height.
4. Ensure filter unit may not disturb to access ports of antenna/RRU

generation

internally or in association with third parties
• Taking appropriate measure to reduce waste in the point of its generation
• Monitoring and measuring all waste, reuse and recycling streams generated,
reporting on trends to staff and senior management
• Fulfil all relevant compliance obligations and other guidance to which the
organization subscribes
• Communicating with staff, customers, partners, contractors, external service
providers, vendors and visitors to ensure that all are aware of the Waste

or harmful health effects to employees
